title: Falling Squares
summary: Given a series of squares with specified positions and side lengths, record the height of the tallest stack of squares after each square is dropped.
statement: Given a series of squares with specified positions and side lengths, record the height of the tallest stack of squares after each square is dropped. Each square falls downward until it lands on the top side of another square or the X-axis, then it freezes in place. Record the height of the tallest stack after each drop.
constraints: 1 <= len(positions) <= 1,000; each square is [left, side length].
Squares stack only when horizontal interiors overlap; touching edges do not overlap. Return global height after each drop.
hints: A falling square rests on the highest earlier square whose horizontal interior overlaps it.
Keep prior half-open intervals and their final heights.
For each [left,right), find maximum height among strict overlaps, add size, then append running maximum.
Earlier squares never move, so direct interval comparison produces the exact support height; half-open boundaries exclude edge touching.
editorial: Earlier squares never move, so direct interval comparison produces the exact support height; half-open boundaries exclude edge touching.

tests.explanation: The first two interiors overlap and stack to height five; the third leaves the global maximum unchanged.
Touching at coordinate 200 does not overlap, so both heights remain one hundred.
